comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred Tax Assets, Liabilities, and Remeasurement
comparisons.peer_summary: Deferred taxes reflect temporary differences, with significant components listed for year-end 2024 and 2023; during 2024, an intercompany integration transaction led to an increase in deferred tax liabilities for acquisition-related intangibles and capitalized R&D, partially offset by a decrease in GILTI liability.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose specific increases in deferred tax liabilities driven by recent acquisitions and integration activities. AVGO explicitly ties $3,642 million in net deferred tax liabilities to the VMware acquisition and a subsequent non-recurring intra-group IP transfer. Similarly, AMD reports that an intercompany integration transaction in 2024 resulted in increases to deferred tax liabilities for acquisition-related intangibles. While AVGO quantifies the specific VMware liability amount, AMD describes the driver (integration transaction) and the nature of the liability (acquisition-related intangibles) without providing a single aggregated dollar figure for the increase in this specific summary text.

sentences.text: As a result of the acquisition of VMware, we established $3,642 million of net deferred tax liabilities on the excess of book basis over the tax basis of acquired assets.
Our net deferred tax liabilities also increased during the year due to the non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States.

During 2024, the Company executed an intercompany integration transaction and remeasured associated deferred taxes, resulting in increases to the deferred tax liability for acquisition-related intangibles and the deferred tax asset for Capitalized R&D, partially offset by a decrease in the deferred tax liability for GILTI.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for INTC focus on the methodology of recognizing deferred taxes (D053) or the establishment of a valuation allowance against deferred tax assets due to historical losses (D108). Neither candidate discusses the creation of new deferred tax liabilities from acquisitions or IP transfers, which is the specific focus of the AVGO disclosure. The INTC disclosures describe passive measurement or asset reversals rather than active liability creation from M&A.

The retrieved candidates for MU focus on the maintenance of a valuation allowance against deferred tax assets (D111) and the status of indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings (D110). These topics concern asset realizability and unremitted earnings, which are conceptually distinct from the creation of deferred tax liabilities resulting from purchase accounting and intra-group IP transfers as disclosed by AVGO.

The retrieved candidates for NVDA describe the general recognition of deferred tax assets/liabilities (D033) and the specific maintenance of a valuation allowance for capital loss carryforwards (D036). Like INTC and MU, these disclosures focus on asset valuation allowances and general methodology, lacking the specific narrative of creating deferred tax liabilities from recent acquisitions or IP transfers found in the AVGO filing.
